source: I want you to create a visual game about a runaway train, it speeds through towns and into objects in its way, you have to speed in reverse to catch up, hook up, and floor it in the other direction, make there be a 10 minute timer and if the timer runs out and the train dosent stop, it derails on a sharp curve and into a river

image_prompt.text: The sharp curve at the end of the line and the river below it — the ground that punishes a train still moving when time runs out
The end of the line at the sharp curve, where the run resolves one way or the other
small towns strung along the track, buildings crowding both sides of the rails
objects standing in the train's way that it smashes through as it speeds along

layout_placement.text: Detection at the sharp curve above the river, resolving the run when the train reaches it
Recovery points restoring a wrecked player vehicle to the track with position, orientation, and zeroed velocity

notes: Forced into Racing. There is no lap and no finish line — the run ends when the train is stopped or when it derails — and this genre's own boundary rule sends a no-lap, no-finish vehicle game to Simulation. Racing was kept because the build is a single continuous route that has to read as one followable line in plan view.
The 10-minute timer and the derailment are the win and loss conditions; neither has a field in this block.

open_questions.ask: What do the towns look like — modern, old-west, industrial?
How many towns does the track pass through before the river, given ten minutes of running time?

coverage_missing.ask: What era and look are the towns?
How long is the track — how many towns before the river?
Does the player win by stopping the train anywhere, or by getting it back to a specific place?

answers.ask: What do the towns look like — modern, old-west, industrial?
answers.answer: Use small industrial railroad towns, with warehouses, loading yards, modest buildings, and trackside obstacles.

answers.ask: How many towns does the track pass through before the river, given ten minutes of running time?
answers.answer: Use three small towns before the river; that keeps the route readable and playable within the ten-minute timer.
